Header:
Date: 2025-03-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jared Collins (CISO, Acme), Priya Nair (Head of Infra, Acme), Liam O'Connor (Cloud Sec Eng, Acme)

Auto-generated Summary (optional):
- Deep dive on encryption at rest and in transit, BYOK options, HSM requirements, key rotation and audit logging.
- Clarified that BYOK/HSM is available on Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted API uses envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS unless customer requests dedicated key isolation.
- Action items: share SOC2/ISO docs, KMS integration guide, schedule POC scoping.

[00:00:00] Sara Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll run about 45 to 60 minutes. This is Sara from Redwood, AE on the account, and Diego is our SE, he'll handle the technical pieces. Jared: thanks for joining.
[00:00:12] Jared Collins: Yeah thanks. Quick intro from our side: I'm Jared, CISO. Priya is Head of Infra, Liam is our cloud security engineer. We're primarily here to validate encryption and key management for a pilot.
[00:00:28] Diego Alvarez: Great, thanks. We'll focus on encryption at rest, in transit, KMS/BYOK options, HSMs, key rotation and audit logs. If we miss anything call it out.
[00:00:45] Priya Nair: Sounds good. We have a few constraints: all customer data at rest must be encrypted with keys we control where possible, and we need audit log exports to our SIEM (Splunk). Also EU data residency for some workloads.
[00:01:05] Sara Kim: Understood. Quick ground rules: for Hosted API there's envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys; BYOK and HSM-backed keys are features we offer for Dedicated and Private deployments. We'll go into options.

--- Topics: Encryption at Rest / Envelope vs BYOK ---

[00:02:02] Diego Alvarez: So at rest we do AES-256-GCM for data on disk. For request payloads and model artifacts we use envelope encryption: our service key encrypts per-customer data keys, which in turn encrypt the objects. For hosted customers that key is Redwood-managed in our KMS.
[00:02:28] Liam O'Connor: When you say Redwood-managed KMS, is that a cloud provider KMS or a proprietary system? I want to understand the trust boundary.
[00:02:38] Diego Alvarez: Good question, uh, by default it's backed by cloud provider KMS — AWS KMS in our primary region — with keys in a Redwood account. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS (CMK) where the key material stays under your control.
[00:02:55] Jared Collins: So for our security policy we need customer control of root key material. Is BYOK fully supported? Do you do key import or key wrapping?
[00:03:07] Diego Alvarez: We support two patterns: Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via key import into the cloud provider's KMS (e.g., import into AWS KMS in the customer's account) and External Key Access (EKM) / key-remotely-stored HSM using CloudHSM or partner HSMs. For BYOK we can accept customer keys imported into the customer's KMS and then we perform envelope encryption where the data key is wrapped by the CMK in the customer's control plane.
[00:03:36] Priya Nair: Clarify: does the Redwood service ever see the plain text key material?
[00:03:43] Diego Alvarez: No. With BYOK via customer KMS import, Redwood never has access to raw key material. We issue requests to the customer's KMS to wrap/unwrap data keys. For EKM/HSM integrations we use a forward proxy pattern so Redwood's runtime calls your HSM endpoint for cryptographic operations.
[00:04:01] Liam O'Connor: Is that only for Private deployments? We're evaluating Dedicated as well. We need the audit trail showing KMS usage in our CloudTrail.
[00:04:11] Sara Kim: BYOK and HSM-backed keys are supported on Dedicated and Private. For Dedicated we can deploy in a VPC with a customer AWS account role that allows Redwood services to call your KMS — that gives you CloudTrail logs for key usage. For hosted customers, it's more limited: Redwood-managed KMS with tenant separation but not full BYOK.

--- Topics: HSM / FIPS / Compliance ---

[00:05:22] Jared Collins: Our procurement requires FIPS 140-2 Level 2/3 for HSM modules and tamper evidence. Do you support that level?
[00:05:33] Diego Alvarez: We can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and partner HSMs). For Private deployments we can support HSMs in your environment. For Dedicated, we typically use CloudHSM clusters in the customer's account if they require FIPS.
[00:05:50] Priya Nair: Is the HSM used for root keys only, or can we configure everything to be HSM-protected?
[00:05:57] Diego Alvarez: Typically root CMKs are HSM-protected; application-level data keys are generated and wrapped by the CMK. We can discuss deeper patterns if you want everything HSM-wrapped — it increases latency for some operations, so it's a tradeoff.

[00:06:35] Liam O'Connor: Latency is a concern. For inference traffic, wrapping/unwrapping per request could add overhead. What's your recommended pattern?
[00:06:45] Diego Alvarez: Recommended pattern is envelope encryption with a short-lived data key cached in-memory in the serving runtime (KV cache). We only call KMS to unwrap when rotating or on cache miss. So normal inference doesn't call the KMS per token. That reduces latency. We have benchmarks showing sub-20ms median extra overhead for typical cache hit scenarios; if you require HSM per-request, you'd see higher tail latencies.

--- Topics: Key Rotation / Lifecycle ---

[00:08:20] Priya Nair: We have a 90-day rotation policy for keys. Can we automate rotation and have Redwood handle re-wrapping with minimal downtime?
[00:08:31] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we support automated key rotation orchestrated from the customer KMS. For BYOK in your account, you can rotate CMKs per your schedule; Redwood will fetch the new key metadata and perform a rolling rewrap of cached data keys. We provide tooling to do a canary rewrap and fallback if anything errors.
[00:08:52] Jared Collins: Is there a requirement for re-encrypting stored objects versus using key versioning?
[00:08:59] Diego Alvarez: We typically use key versioning — new objects are encrypted with the latest data key wrapped by the latest CMK, existing objects maintain older wraps until an explicit re-encrypt is run. We can run bulk rewrap jobs; runtime handles reading older versioned keys. Re-encrypt is optional and can be scheduled.

--- Topics: Audit Logs and SIEM Integration ---

[00:10:20] Priya Nair: We need comprehensive audit logs: KMS operations, key usage, who accessed keys, and data access events. We want these forwarded to Splunk for 13 months.
[00:10:33] Sara Kim: For Dedicated/Private with customer KMS in your account, CloudTrail provides KMS API logs which you own. Redwood can also emit detailed application-level audit events (key request events, dataset access) to your log sink — S3 or direct SIEM integration. We can set retention to 13 months as part of log lifecycle in your account.
[00:10:55] Liam O'Connor: Can we get a sample of the log format? Fields we need: timestamp, key_id, operation, requester_principal, request_id, resource_id, and outcome.
[00:11:05] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll share a sample audit log export. We'll include both KMS-level logs (CloudTrail event) and Redwood application logs with request IDs that map to CloudTrail for correlation.

[00:11:30] Jared Collins: Are there any gaps where logs are only in Redwood's control plane? We need end-to-end visibility.
[00:11:38] Sara Kim: Good point. Our control plane (for hosted) retains some operational logs to manage deployments. For Dedicated/Private, we push all operational logs into your account or a customer-managed logging endpoint. For full isolation, Private with on-prem control plane is the recommended option.

--- Topics: Encryption In Transit / Mutual TLS ---

[00:12:50] Priya Nair: What about in transit? Do you support mTLS and TLS 1.3?
[00:12:56] Diego Alvarez: We use TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred for all client-server traffic. For Dedicated/Private we can configure mutual TLS between your VPC endpoints and Redwood nodes, and we support client cert rotation.

--- Mid-call Clarification and Mis-transcribes ---

[00:14:10] Speaker 1: (laughs) sorry my audio dropped, um, quick nit — does Redwood store plaintext request payloads anywhere?
[00:14:18] Diego Alvarez: No, Redwood does not persist plaintext. We decrypt in-memory in the serving runtime, process, then discard plaintext except where customer chooses to persist outputs; those are re-encrypted.

[00:15:00] Priya Nair: If we run a POC, what's the minimum footprint? We want to try BYOK with a small subset of traffic.
[00:15:08] Sara Kim: We typically do a POC on Dedicated single-AZ with two instances; Diego will draft the minimal architecture — basically customer KMS in your account, a VPC peering or private link, and log sink to your S3.

--- Topics: Regulatory / Data Residency ---

[00:16:40] Jared Collins: We have EU residency requirements for PII — can Redwood ensure data for those tenants never leaves EU?
[00:16:49] Sara Kim: Yes, we can deploy regionally. For hosted customers we have EU regions; for Dedicated/Private we can ensure compute+storage are in EU zones and your KMS resides in EU. Also, customer-managed KMS in your EU account ensures key material never leaves EU.

[00:17:20] Liam O'Connor: Are there any limitations with third-party model variants and BYOK? For example if you want fallback to another model running in a different region.
[00:17:30] Diego Alvarez: If you configure strict residency and BYOK, we block automatic fallback to regions outside the allowed list. We can do model variant fallbacks only within the permitted region and with compatible key setups.

--- Topics: SSO/RBAC and Key Access Controls ---

[00:18:12] Priya Nair: From an operations perspective, how do you handle RBAC? We want to limit which Redwood roles can request key unwrap operations.
[00:18:22] Diego Alvarez: We support granular RBAC in the Console and IAM roles at the infra layer. For Dedicated with customer KMS, the KMS policy in your account controls who can call Decrypt/GenerateDataKey, so you can limit it to a specific role that Redwood assumes. On the Redwood side, we implement least privilege service principals that only perform crypto operations as needed.

[00:19:05] Jared Collins: If an individual engineer at Redwood tries to access keys or logs, what's the guardrail?
[00:19:12] Diego Alvarez: Access requires approved escalation. We have SSO (SAML) with RBAC, audit logs of console/keys access, and break-glass processes logged and requiring multi-approval. We can share our SOC2 controls around privileged access.

--- Deeper technical Q&A ---

[00:20:10] Liam O'Connor: Can we integrate HashiCorp Vault as the external key manager? We run Vault with HSM-backed storage.
[00:20:18] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have a Vault integration pattern where Redwood's runtime calls Vault as the EKM. For performance we recommend Vault sign/unwrap endpoints with a caching layer and leased data keys. Diego: I'll share config snippets.
[00:20:35] Priya Nair: For the HSM approach, do you recommend CloudHSM or external appliance? We're evaluating both.
[00:20:42] Diego Alvarez: CloudHSM in your cloud account is easiest for Dedicated. External appliances are doable for Private or VPN-connected setups, but they'll require network and latency testing.

[00:21:10] Jared Collins: About key revocation — if a key is compromised, what are the steps to rotate and invalidate previous data keys?
[00:21:20] Diego Alvarez: If a CMK is compromised you should rotate or disable it in your KMS. Redwood will stop unwrapping with that CMK and you can run a rewrap to a new CMK. We provide tooling to identify objects using specific key versions to expedite rewrap. We'll also help with revocation playbooks.

--- Performance and Cost Tradeoffs ---

[00:22:55] Liam O'Connor: Any cost implications to using BYOK or HSMs? CloudHSM has per-hour costs and KMS API calls are billed.
[00:23:03] Sara Kim: Correct. BYOK incurs charges for CloudHSM and KMS API usage. We include estimated KMS call counts in our cost model and can recommend batching/caching to reduce per-request costs.

[00:23:45] Priya Nair: Can audit logs be exported in real time for SIEM ingestion? We need near real-time alerts.

[00:23:52] Diego Alvarez: Yes — for Dedicated/Private we can stream logs via Kinesis/Firehose or Kafka connector into your SIEM with <60 second latency in most configurations. For hosted we can push alerts to webhooks but for full control Dedicated/Private is better.

--- Closing: Clarifications and Next Steps ---

[00:25:10] Sara Kim: Quick recap: Redwood supports envelope encryption with AES-256; BYOK/HSM integrations are supported for Dedicated/Private and avoid Redwood having plaintext key material; audit logs can be forwarded to your Splunk/CIEM; we support TLS 1.3 and mTLS in private setups; key rotation and rewrap tooling exists. We'll follow up with docs.
[00:25:35] Jared Collins: Good. Please include the sample CloudTrail/KMS log format, and a diagram of the BYOK flow during the POC. Also confirm that BYOK on Hosted is not available — only on Dedicated/Private.
[00:25:48] Sara Kim: Correct, BYOK on Hosted is limited; we'll document the exact restrictions.

[00:26:10] Diego Alvarez: Action items I'll take: create KMS integration guide for AWS (and notes for GCP/Azure), include Vault and CloudHSM patterns, and share sample log exports.
[00:26:20] Priya Nair: We'll share our current key rotation policy and any compliance checklists.

[00:26:40] Jared Collins: Also can you include your SOC2 Type II timeframe and ISO artifacts for our procurement team?
[00:26:46] Sara Kim: Yes — sending today.

[00:27:10] Speaker 2: (background) we might want a canary before full rewrap just to test performance impact.
[00:27:18] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely, that's our recommended approach.

[00:28:00] Priya Nair: One more question — what about secrets management for API keys and service credentials?
[00:28:07] Sara Kim: Redwood integrates with customer secret stores; for Dedicated/Private we'll use your secret manager or Vault; for hosted we can inject per-tenant secrets but we recommend storing critical credentials in your own secret manager.

[00:29:40] Liam O'Connor: OK. Anything else from Redwood side?
[00:29:44] Sara Kim: No, just that we'll follow up with the POC scope doc and next steps.

[00:30:00] Diego Alvarez: I'll put together an architecture diagram and the sample configuration snippets for your infra team.

[00:30:15] Priya Nair: Timeline: if we agree to POC we want it kicked off mid-March. Can you support that?
[00:30:22] Sara Kim: Yes, week of 2025-03-17 is doable. We'll pencil that in and finalize once we exchange docs.

[00:30:40] Jared Collins: Great. Thanks everyone.

[00:30:45] Sara Kim: Thanks. We'll send the security package and schedule the POC scoping call.
